patterns.name: AWS Access Key
patterns.description: AWS Access Key ID format (AKIA followed by 16 alphanumeric characters)
patterns.detects: Amazon Web Services IAM user access key IDs
patterns.why_it_matters: Compromised AWS keys allow unauthorized access to cloud infrastructure, data stores, and billing.
patterns.remediation: Rotate key immediately in AWS IAM console, check CloudTrail logs for unauthorized activity, and store key in an environment variable or secrets manager.

patterns.name: GitHub Personal Access Token
patterns.description: GitHub Personal Access Token (classic ghp_ or fine-grained github_pat_)
patterns.detects: GitHub Personal Access Tokens (ghp_ or github_pat_)
patterns.why_it_matters: Grants API and repository access depending on token scopes, risking code tampering or repository leaks.
patterns.remediation: Revoke token immediately in GitHub Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens, then generate a new token with minimal scopes.

patterns.name: Stripe Secret Key
patterns.description: Stripe Secret or Restricted API Key
patterns.detects: Stripe live or test secret keys and restricted keys
patterns.why_it_matters: Allows full or scoped access to payment processing, customer details, refunds, and financial transactions.
patterns.remediation: Roll key immediately in the Stripe Dashboard (Developers -> API keys) and verify webhook / charge events.

patterns.name: Private Key
patterns.description: OpenSSL / PEM Private Key header
patterns.detects: PEM formatted RSA, DSA, EC, or OpenSSL private keys
patterns.why_it_matters: Compromising a private key compromises the entire cryptographic identity, allowing impersonation or decryption.
patterns.remediation: Generate a new keypair immediately, replace certificates or SSH authorized_keys on servers, and delete the exposed key.

patterns.name: API Key Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing API_KEY with a non-trivial value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded assignments to api_key or apikey variables with realistic token lengths
patterns.why_it_matters: Hardcoded API keys can be scraped from git repositories or build artifacts and abused by attackers.
patterns.remediation: Move the key to a .env file (added to .gitignore) or retrieve it from an environment variable at runtime.

patterns.name: Secret Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing SECRET or CLIENT_SECRET with a non-trivial value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded assignments to secret or client_secret variables
patterns.why_it_matters: OAuth client secrets or application secrets allow impersonating application services and auth flows.
patterns.remediation: Store secrets in an environment variable or secure secrets manager.

patterns.name: Secret Key Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing SECRET_KEY with a non-trivial value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded assignments to secret_key variables (e.g. Django/Flask SECRET_KEY)
patterns.why_it_matters: Framework secret keys sign session cookies; exposure enables session forgery and remote code execution.
patterns.remediation: Generate a fresh random secret key and inject it through an environment variable.

patterns.name: Password Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing PASSWORD or PWD with a non-trivial value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded plaintext passwords assigned to password, passwd, or pwd variables
patterns.why_it_matters: Plaintext passwords in source code expose user or service accounts to unauthorized access.
patterns.remediation: Change the password immediately and load credentials from environment variables or vault.

patterns.name: Database Password Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing DATABASE_PASSWORD with a non-trivial value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded database passwords in configuration files or code
patterns.why_it_matters: Database access allows direct data exfiltration, tampering, or ransomware encryption.
patterns.remediation: Rotate the database password immediately and inject database credentials via environment variables.

patterns.name: Token Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing TOKEN or AUTH_TOKEN with a non-trivial value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded authentication or access tokens assigned in source code
patterns.why_it_matters: Hardcoded authentication tokens grant direct access to APIs and internal services.
patterns.remediation: Invalidate token, regenerate it, and pass it dynamically via runtime environment variables.

patterns.name: Generic Credential Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment referencing credentials with potential secret
patterns.detects: Short assignments to credential variables that may represent sensitive strings
patterns.why_it_matters: Generic credential strings may leak internal credentials or testing secrets.
patterns.remediation: Verify if the value is sensitive. If sensitive, move to .env; if intentional test fixture, add inline suppression.

patterns.name: Generic Secret Assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment referencing key with potential secret
patterns.detects: Short assignments to key variables that may represent API or service keys
patterns.why_it_matters: Generic keys may be valid tokens for third-party or internal services.
patterns.remediation: Verify if the value is sensitive. If sensitive, move to .env; if placeholder, use recognized placeholder syntax.

patterns.name: AWS Secret Access Key assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY with a 40-character Base64 value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded AWS secret access keys in configuration or code
patterns.why_it_matters: AWS secret keys provide full programmatic access to AWS services, enabling data theft, resource abuse, and infrastructure compromise.
patterns.remediation: Rotate the key immediately in AWS IAM, audit CloudTrail for unauthorized access, and store the key in a secrets manager or environment variable.

patterns.name: AWS Session Token assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing AWS_SESSION_TOKEN with a long Base64 value
patterns.detects: Hardcoded AWS temporary session tokens
patterns.why_it_matters: Session tokens grant temporary AWS access and often accompany leaked access keys, compounding the risk.
patterns.remediation: Revoke the session, rotate associated credentials, and use AWS STS for short-lived tokens injected at runtime.

patterns.name: Google API Key
patterns.description: Google API key starting with AIza prefix
patterns.detects: Google Cloud Platform API keys embedded in source code
patterns.why_it_matters: Leaked Google API keys can be used to consume paid APIs, access restricted data, or impersonate your application.
patterns.remediation: Restrict or delete the key in Google Cloud Console, apply API key restrictions, and load from environment variables.

patterns.name: Google Service Account Key indicator
patterns.description: Google Cloud service account JSON key file structure indicator
patterns.detects: Google Cloud service account private key JSON files committed to source
patterns.why_it_matters: Service account keys grant persistent access to GCP resources and are a common attack vector for cloud compromise.
patterns.remediation: Delete the key from GCP IAM, generate a new key stored outside version control, and use Workload Identity where possible.

patterns.name: Azure Storage Connection String
patterns.description: Azure Storage connection string containing account name and key
patterns.detects: Azure Storage connection strings with embedded access keys
patterns.why_it_matters: Azure Storage connection strings grant full read/write access to blobs, queues, tables, and file shares.
patterns.remediation: Rotate the storage account key in Azure Portal, use Managed Identity or SAS tokens, and store connection strings in Azure Key Vault.

patterns.name: Azure Storage Account Key assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing an Azure Storage account key (86-88 character Base64 value)
patterns.detects: Hardcoded Azure Storage account keys in configuration or code
patterns.why_it_matters: Storage account keys provide unrestricted access to all data in the Azure Storage account.
patterns.remediation: Rotate the key in Azure Portal, migrate to Managed Identity or SAS tokens, and store keys in Azure Key Vault.

patterns.name: GitLab Personal Access Token
patterns.description: GitLab Personal Access Token with glpat- prefix
patterns.detects: GitLab personal or project access tokens
patterns.why_it_matters: GitLab tokens grant API and repository access, risking code theft, pipeline manipulation, and supply chain attacks.
patterns.remediation: Revoke the token in GitLab Settings > Access Tokens, generate a new token with minimal scopes, and use CI/CD variables for automation.

patterns.name: npm Access Token
patterns.description: npm access token or registry authentication token
patterns.detects: npm registry authentication tokens that allow package publishing
patterns.why_it_matters: Compromised npm tokens allow publishing malicious versions of your packages, creating supply chain attacks.
patterns.remediation: Revoke the token at npmjs.com > Access Tokens, generate a new token, and use npm automation tokens with limited scope.

patterns.name: PyPI API Token
patterns.description: PyPI API token with pypi- prefix
patterns.detects: PyPI package index API tokens for publishing Python packages
patterns.why_it_matters: Leaked PyPI tokens allow publishing malicious package versions, enabling widespread supply chain attacks on Python ecosystems.
patterns.remediation: Delete the token at pypi.org > Account Settings > API tokens, generate a new scoped token, and use trusted publishers where possible.

patterns.name: Slack Token
patterns.description: Slack API token (bot, app, user, or service token)
patterns.detects: Slack workspace tokens that provide API access
patterns.why_it_matters: Slack tokens can read messages, post as users, access files, and exfiltrate sensitive communications.
patterns.remediation: Revoke the token in Slack admin, regenerate via your Slack app settings, and store tokens in a secrets manager.

patterns.name: Discord Bot/Webhook Token assignment
patterns.description: Variable assignment containing a Discord bot or webhook token
patterns.detects: Discord bot tokens or webhook URLs embedded in source code
patterns.why_it_matters: Discord tokens allow controlling bots, sending messages, and accessing server data.
patterns.remediation: Regenerate the token in Discord Developer Portal, remove from source code, and use environment variables.

patterns.name: JSON Web Token (JWT)
patterns.description: Signed or encrypted JSON Web Token (JWT) with three Base64URL segments
patterns.detects: JSON Web Tokens used for API authentication, user sessions, and service authorization
patterns.why_it_matters: Leaked JWTs allow attackers to impersonate authorized users or services without requiring passwords.
patterns.remediation: Invalidate the token or rotate signing keys, verify expiration times, and pass tokens dynamically via secure storage or runtime headers.

patterns.name: High Entropy Secret
patterns.description: High Shannon entropy string assigned in credential context
patterns.detects: Unrecognized or custom provider credentials exhibiting high algorithmic randomness
patterns.why_it_matters: High-entropy strings in credential contexts typically represent active API keys, encryption keys, or authentication tokens.
patterns.remediation: Check if the value is an active secret. Move sensitive keys to .env or a secret store; use recognized placeholder syntax for test fixtures.
